title: Moving coil galvanometer, ammeter, and voltmeter
topicTitle: Moving coil galvanometer, ammeter, and voltmeter
notes: A moving-coil galvanometer carries a coil in a radial magnetic field. The torque is N I A B and does not change with angle, because the field is radial. A hairspring supplies a restoring torque k θ.
At rest, N I A B = k θ, so the deflection is proportional to the current. The scale can be marked in equal current steps.
The coil current must stay small. To measure a large current, a low-resistance shunt is connected in parallel with the galvanometer. Most of the current bypasses the coil.
If the galvanometer has resistance G and full-scale current I_g, and the ammeter is to read I, the shunt is S = I_g G / (I − I_g). A larger range needs a smaller shunt.

To make a voltmeter, a large resistor is connected in series. The instrument then draws little current and can be placed across a component. The series resistor is (V / I_g) − G for a full-scale voltage V.
The coil is damped, often by eddy currents in a metal frame, so the needle settles instead of swinging. Swapping the shunt and the series resistor builds the wrong instrument.
